decision: Dropped exact repeats with drop_duplicates(), keeping the first copy.
reason: Identical rows are the same patient entered twice and would repeat patient_id in the joins.

issue: gender spellings that are not a code
decision: Stripped and lowercased, then mapped each spelling to F/M/X; unknown and blank became missing; stored as a category.
reason: Staff typed the same three genders many ways (woman, Male, NB), and unknown does not identify a code.

decision: Uppercased and removed hyphens and spaces so every code reads like N01, S02, or E04.
reason: The same site was typed as n-01, N 01, or S-02, which would split one site into several codes.

decision: Replaced 9999 with missing and stored birth_year as Int64.
reason: 9999 means not recorded, and keeping it would distort birth_year min, max, and ages.

issue: weight column named wt_kg in visits_south.csv
decision: Renamed wt_kg to weight_kg before stacking the two visit files.
reason: The south export used a different column name, so concat would have left two half-empty weight columns.

issue: sbp sentinel 999 and readings outside 70 through 250
decision: Converted to numbers and kept only 70 through 250 mmHg; 999 and out-of-range values became missing.
reason: 999 means not measured and values outside 70 to 250 are not plausible clinic readings.

issue: impossible and loosely written visit dates
decision: Kept a date only when it was exact YYYY-MM-DD text for a real calendar date; anything else became missing.
reason: Slash dates, unpadded months, and impossible dates cannot be read reliably as YYYY-MM-DD.

decision: After mapping visit labels, kept the later reading by visit_time for each patient and visit.
reason: These are rechecks taken minutes apart, and the later reading is the final measurement for that visit.

decision: Kept only current site records, one per site_code, for the join.
reason: N01 and S02 each have a retired name, which would duplicate patients in a many-to-one site join.
